items.event_time_ist: 8:30 PM IST, Oct 13 (Advisory 1, 1500 UTC / 9 AM CST)
items.summary: NHC initiated advisories on Tropical Depression Twenty-One-E (EP212026) off southern Mexico: 35 mph, 1006 mb, ~540 mi SSE of Acapulco, moving NW at 10 mph. No coastal watches/warnings in effect; southwestern and west-central Mexico told to monitor. Forecast is aggressive: hurricane by Wednesday night, major hurricane by Friday (Cat 4, 120 kt/140 mph at day 4 per Discussion 1; models show Cat 4, 36 of 50 DeepMind members Cat 4+). NHC notes the cyclone could be 'very close to the coast of Mexico as a hurricane over the weekend,' with several ensemble members showing landfall in southwestern or west-central Mexico; swells reaching southern Mexico late week. Next Pacific name is Trudy once it strengthens to a tropical storm.
items.title: Tropical Depression Twenty-One-E forms off southern Mexico; NHC forecasts rapid intensification to a major hurricane by Friday
